priorIterationFindingReconfirmation.FIND-1201: GENUINELY RESOLVED. Read REQ-103's own EARS clause (behavioral-spec.md:680-689), its statePath prose (behavioral-spec.md:700-733, specifically 716-719), and its Acceptance Criteria (behavioral-spec.md:757-765) side by side: all three now state the IDENTICAL scope verbatim -- 'the lock is held from REQ-201's wallet generation THROUGH REQ-305's ledger append actually completing' -- with the EARS clause and Acceptance Criteria each explicitly cross-referencing the other two ('resolves FIND-1201: no "and beyond" open-ended phrasing, and no narrower reading that releases the lock any earlier'). No residual 'and beyond' open-ended phrasing or narrower 'REQ-201 through REQ-205, and the decision to proceed into REQ-3xx' phrasing remains anywhere outside the changelog's own historical description of the original bug (grepped both spec files for 'and beyond' and 'decision to proceed into REQ-3xx' -- only changelog/RESOLUTION-NOTES occurrences found). PROP-103e (verification-architecture.md:276) is a genuinely distinct fixture from PROP-103a (verification-architecture.md:272): PROP-103a proves interlock under a SIMULTANEOUS race (both evaluators observe eligible:true at the same instant); PROP-103e proves the lock remains held under a STAGGERED race where a second evaluator's lock-acquire attempts are issued repeatedly WHILE a first evaluator's REQ-304 funding call is deliberately delayed (i.e. strictly AFTER the first evaluator's REQ-201-205 have already completed) -- this genuinely exercises the specific failure mode reading (3) of the original three-way inconsistency would have permitted (the lock releasing early, between REQ-205 and REQ-305), which PROP-103a's simultaneous-race fixture structurally cannot exercise (a simultaneous race can pass even if the lock is held for only a few milliseconds, since both racers start at t0). The Gate's item (2) (verification-architecture.md:600-615) correctly requires PROP-103e 'IN ADDITION to PROP-103a's simultaneous-race fixture, since a simultaneous race alone cannot prove the lock is not released early somewhere between REQ-206 and REQ-305.' REQ-304's Acceptance Criteria (behavioral-spec.md:1901-1914) also correctly reflects the corrected lock scope by depending on REQ-101's per-citizen function being computed while the lock is genuinely held through the funding step.
priorIterationFindingReconfirmation.FIND-1202: GENUINELY RESOLVED. REQ-101's body (behavioral-spec.md:447-464) specifies `computePerCitizenSurplusUsd({citizens, perCitizenReserveUsd}) -> Array<{citizenId, surplusUsd}>` as a new sibling pure function in the same file as `computeColonySurplusUsd`, and explicitly states `computeColonySurplusUsd` 'SHALL be implemented by CALLING this function and summing its returned surplusUsd values -- never by an independently-written, separately-maintained reduce.' REQ-101's Acceptance Criteria (behavioral-spec.md:549-554) restates this by-construction relationship. REQ-304's own Acceptance Criteria (behavioral-spec.md:1909-1914) now explicitly binds the per-transfer ceiling check to this function BY NAME: 'read directly, by name, from REQ-101's computePerCitizenSurplusUsd({citizens, perCitizenReserveUsd}) output for that citizen's citizenId (never an independently re-derived or re-summed aggregate value)' -- this is the exact binding-by-name the iteration-13 review found missing. verification-architecture.md's Purity Boundary Map row (line 119) and PROP-101i (line 266) both specify the identical by-construction relationship and require a Tier-0 structural check (computeColonySurplusUsd's source literally calls computePerCitizenSurplusUsd and sums it) plus a Tier-1 fixture test proving per-citizen correctness AND aggregate-sum consistency on the same fixture; PROP-304f (line 331) is updated to read 'from REQ-101's computePerCitizenSurplusUsd(...) output for that citizen's citizenId,' and Gate items (1e)/(7) (lines 591-598, 677-696) both require the adversary to confirm this binding. No independently re-derived or re-summed parallel computation of the per-citizen term was found anywhere in either spec file.
